message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta.** Noise complaints are handled by the city’s public‑safety and code‑enforcement offices, not directly by the city council. The council can refer the issue to the appropriate department, but the actual complaint is processed through the city’s official channels. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1. Identify the type of noise** | • Residential or commercial
• Daytime (8 a.m.–10 p.m.) vs. nighttime (10 p.m.–8 a.m.)
• Persistent vs. one‑off | – | | **2. Contact the City’s 311 Service** | • Phone: **404‑656‑3111** (or dial 311 from any Atlanta phone)
• Online: https://311.atlantaga.gov | 311 will route your complaint to the correct department. | | **3. File an online complaint** | • Use the City of Atlanta’s “Noise Complaint” portal:
https://www.atlantaga.gov/311/noise-complaint | – | | **4. Email or mail a written complaint** | • Email: **noise@atlantaga.gov**
• Mail: City of Atlanta, 311 Office, 1000 Peachtree Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30308 | – | | **5. Call the Atlanta Police Department (APD) – Noise Enforcement Unit** | • Phone: **404‑656‑3111** (same as 311) or **404‑656‑3111** for the Noise Enforcement Unit specifically | – | | **6. If the issue is a code violation** | • Contact the City of Atlanta’s Code Enforcement Division:
Phone: **404‑656‑3111** or **404‑656‑3111** (via 311) | – | ### What Happens Next? 1. **Investigation** – A city officer will investigate the complaint. 2. **Enforcement** – If the noise violates the city’s Noise Ordinance, the officer may issue a warning, citation, or order to cease the activity. 3. **Follow‑up** – You’ll receive a notice of the outcome (usually via mail or email). --- ## Relevant Laws & Ordinances | Law / Ordinance | Key Points | Where to Find It | |-----------------|------------|------------------| | **City of Atlanta Noise Ordinance** | • Sets permissible decibel limits for residential and commercial areas.
• Defines “quiet hours” (10 p.m.–8 a.m.).
• Provides penalties for violations. | https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety/department-of-public-safety-division-of-traffic-and-transportation/noise-ordinance | | **Georgia Code Title 43, Chapter 7 – Noise** | • State law that supports local noise ordinances.
• Provides a framework for enforcement. | https://law.justia.com/codes/georgia/2023/title-43/chapter-7/ | --- ## Quick Tips - **Document the noise**: Record the time, duration, and type of noise (e.g., music, construction, barking dogs). - **Check the neighborhood’s zoning**: Some areas allow higher noise levels (e.g., commercial zones). - **Use the online portal**: It’s faster than calling and keeps a record of your complaint. - **Follow up**: If you don’t hear back within a week, call 311 to check the status. --- ### Bottom Line You can definitely report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. Use the 311 system, the online portal, or email/phone the Noise Enforcement Unit. The city council itself does not process complaints directly, but they can refer the matter to the appropriate department. If you need more detailed legal information, consult the City of Atlanta Noise Ordinance or the Georgia Code.
